cases.title: Establishment-only KEL
cases.description: An inception with the EO trait, then an interaction, then a rotation at sequence number 1. A validator must drop the interaction (line 377) and should accept the rotation.

cases.title: Establishment-only delegator anchoring in an interaction
cases.description: A delegator incepted with the EO trait anchors a delegated inception in an interaction. A validator must drop the interaction, so the delegating seal is never seen and it must not accept the delegated inception (line 1612).

cases.title: Delegation from a do-not-delegate delegator
cases.description: A delegator incepted with the DND trait anchors a delegated inception in an interaction. The validator holds the delegator's KEL when the delegated inception arrives, so it must drop it (line 379).

cases.title: Rotation carrying the establishment-only trait
cases.description: An inception with no traits, then a rotation whose configuration traits are [EO], signed by the exposed next key, then an interaction at sequence number 1 chained to the inception. EO may appear only in an inception (lines 367 and 371), and a validator must drop an event that breaks its traits' constraints (line 367), so it must drop the rotation. Nothing then makes the KEL establishment-only, and the interaction should be accepted on the inception's keys.

dispute.summary: keripy main reads configuration traits only from an identifier's inception (Kever.config is called when the Kever is created, never from Kever.update), so it accepts a rotation that carries EO, DND or DID as if its traits were empty, applies the rotation to the key state, and treats a later event at the rotation's sequence number as duplicitous.
dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-15; not yet raised with keripy or the KERI specification working group.

cases.title: Rotation carrying the do-not-delegate trait
cases.description: A delegator's inception with no traits, then a rotation of the delegator whose configuration traits are [DND], then an interaction of the delegator chained to its inception that anchors a delegated inception. DND may appear only in an inception (lines 367 and 372), so a validator must drop the rotation (line 367). The delegator therefore never acquires the trait, and the delegated inception, anchored by a seen interaction, should be accepted.

dispute.summary: keripy main reads configuration traits only from an identifier's inception (Kever.config is called when the Kever is created, never from Kever.update), so it accepts a rotation that carries EO, DND or DID as if its traits were empty, applies the rotation to the key state, and treats a later event at the rotation's sequence number as duplicitous.
dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-15; not yet raised with keripy or the KERI specification working group.

cases.title: Rotation carrying the delegate-is-delegator trait
cases.description: An inception, then a rotation whose configuration traits are [DID], signed by the exposed next key. DID may appear only in an inception (lines 367 and 373), so a validator must drop the rotation (line 367), and the key state stays the inception's.

dispute.summary: keripy main reads configuration traits only from an identifier's inception (Kever.config is called when the Kever is created, never from Kever.update), so it accepts a rotation that carries EO, DND or DID as if its traits were empty, applies the rotation to the key state, and treats a later event at the rotation's sequence number as duplicitous.

cases.title: Delegated rotation carrying the establishment-only trait
cases.description: A delegator and a delegated inception it anchors, then a delegated rotation whose configuration traits are [EO], anchored by a second interaction of the delegator. Line 367 applies to inception-only traits on delegated events as well ("delegated or not"), so a validator must drop the delegated rotation, although its seal is seen, and the delegate's key state stays its inception's.
